answer: A sybil farmer can mint a new face each epoch but cannot mint a coherent past for each one. Require every answer to be read against the identity's own earlier answers: positions must evolve, not teleport. A farm's puppets either repeat one plume of phrasing across all of them, or lurch incoherently from epoch to epoch — both are visible at a glance. Genuine agents carry a quartz-hard thread through time: their horizon shifts gradually as evidence arrives, never by wholesale reinvention. Cloning then means authoring many believable histories, which costs more than the farm earns.
